newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX charts flag possible retracement.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX charts flag possible retracement.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* Technicals for NYMEX futures are flagging a possible retracement of Tuesdays losses, but fundamentals remain weak. * Chart patterns show that the markets downside has been arrested although there is still no clear indication the bulls are in charge again.
Technicals for NYMEX oil futures are flagging a possible retracement of Tuesday's losses, but fundamentals remain weak, analysts and brokers said.

The final hammer formation of Tuesday's trading range on the front month continuation chart for unleaded gasoline, following the dip from last Fridays high of 67.60 cents a gallon, may suggest that the markets downside has been arrested, analysts said.
But there is still no clear indication the bulls are in charge again.

According to Japanese candlestick charting techniques the formation of a Doji candlestick today, with trading expected to remain quiet and in a narrow range ahead of the delayed API U.S. stock figures, could flag a retracement of Tuesday's losses.
Crude charts show a similar pattern but analysts say here any retracement will depend on a tug from gasoline.

However lurking in the background is the perception that fundamentals are growing consistently weaker. "The biggest surprise was the fall in gasoline which traditionally is the strongest contract at this time of year due to the start of the driving season," said Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives.
"The feeling is production rates are currently so high that supply should easily cover demand. It therefore looks as if today could be a typical pre-API day, quiet and sideways," she added.
Neither crude oil inventories nor refinery capacity utilisation rates are expected to have declined significantly from last week's levels, brokers said on Tuesday.

Crude typically looks for demand in unleaded gasoline during peak summer driving periods, and although unleaded inventories are about seven million barrels below last year's levels, crude inventories and refinery utilisation in the U.S. is still high.

"A lot depends on what products do, and right now the products are coming off. Unless gasoline can take the ball and run with it, over time the fundamentals are less favourable," said Smith Barney analyst John Saucer.

Profit margins have begun to decline significantly in Asia and Europe, which has caused some major refiners to begin scaling back production, a development that does not bode well for the industry's expectations of upcoming demand.
NYMEX July crude futures breached a succession of key chart points during its decline Tuesday.
They included the 10-day moving average of $21.61 and the 20-day moving average of $20.81, where support was expected to be strong.
The next key technical support level for July crude was seen in the area of $20.50.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
